related_questions.question: What level of ferritin is concerning?

text_blocks.snippet: Ferritin levels above 300 ng/mL in men and above 200 ng/mL in women are generally considered elevated and may be concerning, potentially indicating iron overload or other underlying conditions. Conversely, levels below 40 ng/mL are typically considered low, suggesting iron deficiency. However, some individuals may experience symptoms of iron deficiency even with slightly higher ferritin levels (around 100 ng/mL).
snippet_highlighted_words: above 300 ng/mL in men and above 200 ng/mL in women

list.snippet: Below 40 ng/mL: Generally considered low and indicative of iron deficiency.
Below 100 ng/mL: May cause symptoms in some individuals, particularly those with conditions like restless legs syndrome.
Above 300 ng/mL in men and above 200 ng/mL in women: These levels are generally considered elevated.
Above 1000 ng/mL: May be associated with hemochromatosis and other conditions like liver disease or inflammation, according to healthcare resources.

list.title: Individual Variation:
list.snippet: Normal ranges can vary between laboratories and also depend on age and gender.

list.title: Inflammation:
list.snippet: Inflammation can cause ferritin levels to be falsely elevated, even without iron overload.

list.title: Underlying Conditions:
list.snippet: High or low ferritin levels can be a sign of various underlying conditions, including anemia, hemochromatosis, and liver disease.

list.title: Further Testing:
list.snippet: If ferritin levels are outside the normal range, further testing may be necessary to determine the underlying cause and appropriate treatment.
